title: Fairy Cakes vs Cupcakes: What's the Difference?
summaryShort: Fairy cakes are small British sponge cakes with a thin glacé icing, while cupcakes are larger American-style cakes with a tall swirl of buttercream. Both are baked in cases, and the batter is often very similar.
metaTitle: Fairy Cakes vs Cupcakes: The Difference
metaDescription: Fairy cakes vs cupcakes explained for UK and US bakers: size, batter, icing, cases and butterfly cakes. Read the guide and bake the right one.
sidebarTitle: Fairy Cakes vs Cupcakes at a Glance
sidebarBullets: Fairy cakes are smaller, around 2 tablespoons of batter each.
Cupcakes use about 3 to 4 tablespoons of batter.
Fairy cakes get thin glacé icing or a light dusting of sugar.
Cupcakes get a tall swirl of buttercream.
UK says cases, US says liners. They are the same thing.
Butterfly cakes are the classic fairy cake variation.

sections.heading: What Is the Main Difference?
paragraphs: Size and topping are the main differences. A fairy cake is a small, light sponge with a flat layer of icing, and a cupcake is bigger with a tall swirl of frosting.
The words overlap a lot, especially online. In my kitchen, I use "fairy cake" when I want something dainty for tea, and "cupcake" when I want a showstopper.
list: Fairy cakes: small, plain, thin icing.

sections.heading: Size and How Much Batter to Use
paragraphs: Fairy cakes use about 2 tablespoons of batter, while cupcakes use 3 to 4 tablespoons. A fairy cake fits a small case in a shallow bun tin, and a cupcake fills a muffin cup two thirds full.

The smaller size changes the bake. Fairy cakes are done in 10 to 15 minutes at 350°F (180°C, or 160°C fan), while cupcakes need 18 to 22 minutes. Check fairy cakes early, because small cakes dry out fast.

sections.heading: The Batter: British Sponge vs American-Style
paragraphs: Both usually start with creamed butter and sugar, but they lean differently. A classic British fairy cake is a simple sponge with equal weights of butter, sugar, eggs and self-raising flour, so it is light, plain and slightly firm.
American-style cupcake batter often adds milk, buttermilk or sour cream. That makes a softer, moister, more tender crumb that can carry a heavy frosting without feeling dry.
list: British sponge: butter, sugar, eggs, self-raising flour.
American-style: adds milk or buttermilk, often more vanilla.
Sponge is lighter and drier, American style is softer and richer.

sections.heading: Icing: Glacé vs Buttercream
paragraphs: Fairy cakes usually wear glacé icing, which is just powdered sugar mixed with a little water or lemon juice. It sets into a thin, shiny, slightly crisp layer that you spoon on and leave flat.

Cupcakes get buttercream, made by beating butter with powdered sugar until fluffy, then piping it in a tall swirl. Buttercream is richer and goes on much thicker, so it pairs best with a moist, tender cake.
list: Glacé icing: 1 cup powdered sugar plus 1 to 2 tablespoons water or lemon juice.
Buttercream: 1 cup butter plus 3 to 4 cups powdered sugar and a splash of milk.

sections.heading: Cases vs Liners (and Why It Does Not Matter)
paragraphs: Cases and liners are the same paper cup, just a different word. UK bakers say paper cases, US bakers say cupcake liners.
Size is what matters. Use small cases for fairy cakes in a shallow bun tin, and standard liners in a muffin pan for cupcakes. A cake baked in a case that is too big spreads thin and bakes flat.

sections.heading: Butterfly Cakes: The Classic Fairy Cake
paragraphs: A butterfly cake is a fairy cake with the top sliced off, cut in half and set back like wings. You fill the gap with buttercream or whipped cream, and often a spoon of jam.
To make one, cut a small circle from the top using a sharp knife. Fill the dip, then press the two halves in at an angle. A light dusting of powdered sugar finishes it nicely.

howToSteps: Decide the size: use about 2 tablespoons of batter for fairy cakes, 3 to 4 for cupcakes.
Choose the batter: simple sponge for fairy cakes, or add milk or buttermilk for a softer cupcake.
Fill small cases for fairy cakes or standard liners for cupcakes, about two thirds full.
Bake fairy cakes 10 to 15 minutes and cupcakes 18 to 22 minutes at 350°F (180°C).
Cool completely before topping, or the icing will melt and slide off.
Spoon glacé icing on fairy cakes, or pipe a tall swirl of buttercream on cupcakes.
For butterfly cakes, cut a circle from the top, fill it, and set the halves back as wings.

faq.question: Are fairy cakes and cupcakes the same thing?
faq.answer: Not quite. They are close cousins, but fairy cakes are smaller with thin icing, while cupcakes are bigger with tall frosting. Many people use the names interchangeably.

faq.question: Can I use a cupcake recipe to make fairy cakes?
faq.answer: Yes. Use less batter per case, about 2 tablespoons, and shorten the bake to 10 to 15 minutes. Then top with glacé icing instead of buttercream.

faq.question: What is a butterfly cake?
faq.answer: It is a fairy cake with the top cut off, sliced in half and placed back like wings. It is filled with buttercream or cream and sometimes jam.

faq.question: Do I need a special tin for fairy cakes?
faq.answer: No. A standard muffin pan works with small cases, or use a shallow 12-hole bun tin. Use less batter so the cakes stay small.

faq.question: Can I put buttercream on a fairy cake?
faq.answer: Yes, nobody will stop you. It just turns it into a small cupcake, so use a small piping nozzle and keep the swirl low.
